images.method: image generation with D24P11A as visual reference (single generator model)
images.prompt: Create ONE standalone overhead game-map composition, not a collage or UI. Treat the attached PMD reference ONLY as a guide for its deep moss-green grass, gnarled brown tree roots with fluffy green crowns, stone cobble path beige, small grey mossy rocks, and crisp Pokemon Mystery Dungeon pixel-art language; invent a wholly new layout. Landscape 4:3 composition, 1200 by 896 pixels, wide and zoomed out, strict top-down orthographic view, readable at native 8-pixel tile scale. A new forest entrance map: the player enters from the south/lower-center, follows a clear stone cobble path with two gentle bends northward, then reaches one dark arched cave threshold at the upper-center. Keep a continuous uncluttered corridor at least three tiles wide; roots, trees and rocks never block it. Build a distinctive asymmetric forest: dense lush mossy ground cover, scattered small grey stones, gnarled ancient trees with round lollipop canopies and twisting exposed roots, tiny pink and yellow flowers, subtle dappled light. Give the northern cave mouth a readable deep static shadow under knotted roots, not a portal or door. The map's landmass reaches all four image edges behind the dense tree walls, so no transparent border. Use deep moss green, forest green, bark brown, stone beige and soft flower accents faithfully related to the reference palette; do not copy its exact composition. Clean hard pixel clusters, no blur, no antialiasing, no painterly gradients. Absolutely no characters, signs, text, labels, UI, border, watermark, water, lava, snow, ice, crystals. No magenta in the artwork itself.

The entire image must be floor only, edge to edge, with slight variations in moss tone and scattered tiny ground speckles. Keep the main floor tone and texture consistent with the map and PMD reference. No trees, roots, rocks, flowers, cave mouth, shadows, water, magenta, text, border, blur, crop, camera change, perspective change. This is a separate aligned source layer, not a new layout.
